Yes, CVS Health sells select consumer fitness and health-monitoring smartwatches and wellness-related tracking devices through
CVS Pharmacy
retail channels and its website
, though it primarily acts as a traditional retail distributor for third-party brands rather than a manufacturer of clinical-grade medical wearables.
CliffsNotes

CVS Health does not manufacture a dedicated continuous glucose monitor (CGM), smartwatch, or wearable ECG ring/patch
. Instead, CVS over-the-counter health offerings feature traditional blood glucose meters like the
CVS Health Advanced Bluetooth Glucose Meter
, while broader enterprise arms like Signify Health provide clinical-grade remote 14-day ECG arrhythmia patch monitoring.
CVS Health
CVS Health At-Home Devices & Remote Care
Blood Glucose Meters:
Traditional fingerstick readers (e.g., CVS Advanced Bluetooth Meter) connect with mobile apps to log data, but they require manual blood drops rather than continuous interstitial tracking.
Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM):
CVS Health utilizes data platforms and analytics through programs like Transform Diabetes Care to track blood pressure and glucose metrics.
CVS Health
Wearable ECG Services:
Signify Health (a CVS Health company) deploys professional 14-day continuous ECG patches for in-home cardiac arrhythmia and Atrial Fibrillation (AFib) screening.
CVS Health
Commercial Wearables Alternatives
If you are looking for true continuous passive tracking outside of CVS store brands:
Continuous Glucose Monitors:
Brand options like Abbott's Freestyle Libre or Dexcom G7 provide real-time transdermal tracking.
Smartwatches & Wearable ECG:
Devices from Apple, Fitbit, or Samsung offer on-demand ECG recordings and passive heart-rate/sleep analytics.
